Support protein structure intelligence, variant effects/interpretation, functional genomics, pharmacogenomics, gene–drug and genotype–phenotype relationships, and molecular pathways. A laboratory supplies authorized reports and QC; a qualified genetics/molecular reviewer assesses clinical relevance; a researcher uses separately authorized datasets; the patient controls available access/delegation under applicable policy. Neither a scientific service identity nor a general chatbot may authorize a clinical interpretation.

CAP-LABORATORY retains tests/results; CAP-DATA retains patient-linked clinical records and genomic report references. The adapter stores execution metadata and derived artifacts under CAP-AI. Input may reference approved sequence/variant files, reference assembly, transcript and version, coordinate convention, alleles, zygosity/phase where known, sample/tissue, germline/somatic/pathogen context, quality flags and pipeline release. Human and pathogen genomes are distinct datasets with distinct identity implications.

Protein requests include sequence/reference version, isoform, model task and intended use. Output includes provider/model version, task, input digest, returned artifact, confidence semantics, limitations, reference dataset/license, provenance and approval state. Structure prediction, functional effect prediction and clinical actionability are three separate result types. Do not infer drug benefit from a predicted fold.

Registry entry pins provider, API/model version, accepted formats, data residency, retention/training terms, license, intended-use evaluation and fallback eligibility. No clinical provider is configured by this document.

Validate consent/purpose and legal basis → minimize data → check provider eligibility → submit idempotent job → quarantine output → check schema/provenance/QC → specialist review where required → release a typed result. Cancellation/timeout does not erase the audit trail. A change of model/provider starts a new derived artifact; it does not silently overwrite an interpretation.

Revision 2026-09-14 · EXT-AI · DRAFT_SPECIFICATION · CAP-AI · shared AI infrastructure / governed inference and learning · roadmap RESEARCH.

Provide one infrastructure with task-specific policy, provenance and evaluation. Existing 1369 already calls for model version, dataset, approval and performance; 1259 requires clinical validation/version/safety; 1218 retraining and 1547 knowledge learning need separate controlled release paths. Specialty AI titles become candidate profiles with prompts, retrieval scope, evaluation sets and permissions. They do not automatically receive their own gateways, model registries or patient stores.

Knowledge AI retrieves and explains approved evidence with source/version and applicability. Clinical AI supports authorized clinician decisions within a validated intended use. Personal AI provides patient-facing explanations and navigation with no autonomous prescribing or diagnosis. Research AI works within protocol/dataset/disclosure permissions and emits hypotheses rather than clinical knowledge.

The shared platform supplies AI Gateway, Model Router, RAG, Clinical Knowledge Graph, Model Registry, Evaluation, Safety, Monitoring, Audit, Provenance, Uncertainty and Human Review. Knowledge ownership belongs to approved evidence releases; source clinical facts stay with clinical services.

A task owner specifies use, risk class, input sensitivity, patient/tenant/purpose, jurisdiction, latency/cost limits and required validation. Model stewards approve releases; clinical governance approves clinical intended use; privacy/security approves processing terms. Execution service identities cannot approve themselves.

RouteRequest references authorized context, evidence pack, task/profile version and processing policy. ModelRelease declares provider/model version, task eligibility, populations/exclusions, evaluation, region, retention/training terms, context limits, tool permissions, approval and rollback target. RouteDecision records eligible candidates, exclusions, selected release, policy version and rationale.

First apply hard constraints: task/intended use, clinical risk, privacy, jurisdiction and validation. Only then optimize among eligible routes for latency and cost. A timeout can switch only to a separately approved route for the same task, data and population. Otherwise abstain or defer to a human. A cheaper model is never an automatic substitute.

Adapters may eventually support OpenAI, Google/DeepMind, Anthropic, xAI, open-source, specialized biomedical and future EDHT models. These are illustrative provider categories, not configured or validated integrations. Business contracts use EDHT task/result envelopes, not provider-specific chat objects. Keep provider translation, rate limits and output parsing within adapters.

Proposed commands: executeGovernedTask, evaluateCandidateRelease, recordHumanReview, approveModelRelease, revokeModelRelease. Events InferenceCompleted, ModelAbstained, ReviewRequested, ModelReleaseChanged and OutputInvalidated contain artifact/version references. Idempotency and explicit cancellation prevent duplicate consequential tool actions. This stage creates no deployed endpoints or provider credentials.

Retrieval enforces authorization before indexing/querying and on source access; embedding stores inherit source sensitivity and deletion/revocation policy. Evidence snippets are untrusted content, never execution instructions. Index releases pin corpus/terminology versions. The knowledge graph preserves provenance, conflicting claims, applicability and review state.

Result envelope records source IDs, model release, prompt/task version, retrieval version, epistemic status, uncertainty representation, limitations and human disposition. Unsupported claims trigger abstention. Model confidence is not a calibrated probability unless evaluation supports that interpretation. Tool calls pass through deterministic authorization and schema validation; recommendations cannot call a medication mutation tool.

Enforce minimum necessary context, separate consent/legal-basis/purpose checks, tenant isolation, provider retention/region rules and redacted logging. Test prompt injection from documents, exfiltration, cross-patient context, stale retrieval, tool misuse, bias/subgroup performance and unsupported age/language. Model outage, schema mismatch or revoked release returns an explicit unavailable state; it must not fabricate a result or select an unapproved provider.

Monitor safety incidents, drift, abstention rate, latency, cost, evaluation regressions and human overrides against defined denominators. Pin releases and retain traceability; emergency disablement invalidates affected derived outputs while preserving audit.

Clinical data → governed dataset → evaluation/research → permitted model improvement → validation → signed release → monitoring. Every training/export step requires an approved basis, purpose and retention policy. Feedback is evidence for review, not an automatic training grant. Knowledge-pack updates and model retraining have separate releases.

Acceptance tests must demonstrate hard-constraint routing before optimization, approved fallback or abstention, source-linked explanations, refusal of clinical fact/order writes, and replayable model/context versions. Dependencies CAP-DATA, CAP-CONSENT, CAP-AUDIT; downstream CDS/twin/research consume typed results. Open gates: model/task evaluation suites, provider contracts, clinical authority, incident response ownership and patient-facing human-factors validation.

A patient supplies reported exposure and symptoms; a treating clinician reconciles source records and reviews recommendations; a pharmacist reviews interactions; a qualified genetics reviewer adjudicates PGx interpretation. Research staff receive separate governed datasets. A service identity may read only the episode and purpose authorized by the consent/access service.

Workflow: reconcile medication history → freeze context → validate applicability and missingness → retrieve evidence → calculate an approved assessment/scenario → expose uncertainty and alternatives → clinician accepts, rejects or requests more evidence. An accepted recommendation still requires a separate authenticated medication order, with its own author and lifecycle. No AI or twin service may issue or change that order.

CAP-MEDICATION owns medication statements, reconciliation and exposure episodes, with references to prescriptions owned by CAP-PRESCRIPTION, dispensing owned by CAP-PHARMACY and administration owned by CAP-ADMINISTRATION. CAP-DATA owns identity-linked clinical context; CAP-LABORATORY owns results and CAP-CDS owns derived assessments. CAP-AI owns model execution provenance, not medication truth.

The context snapshot includes age and date basis, sex-related clinical context where relevant, height, weight, BSA plus formula/input versions, diagnoses, chronic disease, allergies, prior adverse reactions, current and past medicines, active ingredients, strength/formulation, route, dose units, frequency, start/stop times and adherence uncertainty. Provides a centralized gateway for secure communication with external healthcare, payment and third-party services.

Revision 2026-09-14 · EXT-INTEROP · DRAFT_SPECIFICATION · CAP-INTEROP · integration and transformation / external clinical systems · roadmap RESEARCH.

Reduce manual integration work while preserving clinical meaning and source authority. Existing 1356 lists HL7/FHIR/DICOM/CDA and 1359 universal connectors; numerous synchronization titles describe intent. They do not specify safe discovery, semantic validation, loss budgets and release control. Extend this owner using the [search dossier](new_module_proposals.json); do not treat an absent title as proof of an absent capability.

Partner administrator authorizes scope and read-only credentials; an integration engineer inspects schemas; a terminology steward adjudicates concepts; the clinical data owner approves clinical semantics; an operator deploys an approved version. Approval policy must prevent a generated connector from approving itself.

Accept FHIR, HL7 v2, CDA, DICOM, CSV, JSON, XML, REST APIs, authorized database exports and vendor-specific formats where technically and legally permitted. Format recognition is not conformance. Each partner declares protocol/version, purpose, data authority, direction, frequency, volume and authorization boundary. No unauthorised scanning, external writes, destructive SQL or automatic schema migration.
1. Read-only Connector Discovery inventories only authorized endpoints/files.
2. Format Detection identifies candidate encodings, delimiters/protocols and versions.
3. Schema Profiling records types, cardinalities, missingness, units, identifiers and sample provenance in a restricted staging area.
4. Semantic Mapping proposes source concepts and meaning; Terminology Mapping pins systems/releases; FHIR Mapping selects explicit profiles and extensions.
5. Validation checks syntax, identity/tenant, units, time zones, value sets, cardinality, required fields and authority.
6. Conflict Detection separates duplicate messages, patient ambiguity, contradictory results and corrected versions.
7. Transformation produces quarantined canonical candidates plus loss reports.
8. Sandbox Testing uses synthetic/de-identified approved fixtures, error cases and round-trip checks.
9. Human Approval signs exact schema/mapping/connector versions and a bounded release scope.
10. Connector Registry publishes the signed release; Monitoring detects drift, loss, rejection and reconciliation failures.
11. Rollback stops intake and restores a known connector release; already accepted clinical records require attributable correction/compensation, never silent deletion.

CAP-INTEROP owns ConnectorProfile, MappingCandidate, MappingRelease, ImportBatch and LossReport. Clinical owners retain validated facts. MappingCandidate contains source field/path, source schema hash, target concept/profile, transformation, confidence method/value, evidence source, terminology release, validation state, reviewer decision, approval scope and version. Confidence alone never authorizes import.

ImportBatch records input digest, partner/message identity, patient-match result, mapping release, item outcomes and idempotency key. A write candidate must reference approved source authority, validated mapping and current release. The clinical owner revalidates and accepts it; the connector cannot unilaterally overwrite the source of truth.

Proposed commands: discoverAuthorizedSchema, proposeMapping, validateMapping, runSandbox, approveConnectorRelease, stageImport, reconcileBatch, suspendConnector. Signed approvals bind artifact hashes. Events MappingProposed, ValidationFailed, ConnectorReleaseApproved, ImportQuarantined, ImportAccepted and ConnectorDriftDetected contain identifiers and counts.

Return AMBIGUOUS_PATIENT, UNKNOWN_UNIT, LOSS_EXCEEDS_POLICY, UNAPPROVED_MAPPING, SCHEMA_DRIFT or STALE_RELEASE as appropriate. Per-item quarantine must not mask batch failures. Retries use stable partner event IDs and source versions. Out-of-order corrections retain linkage to earlier results.

AI can propose probable concepts, missing-field handling and candidate connector code/tests. Generated code is untrusted: sandbox it without production credentials, review dependencies and prevent network escape. It cannot approve its own test expectations. Unknown or incompatible semantics remain unresolved. Round-trip tests compare both retained fields and clinically meaningful semantics; where reverse conversion is impossible, record explicit loss and block or require approved limits.

Use secret management outside repository, least privilege, transport encryption, restricted staging retention, access audit, consent/purpose checks and jurisdiction controls. Logs include schema/release hashes and rejection counts, not sample PHI. Dependencies CAP-DATA, CAP-IDENTITY, CAP-CONSENT, CAP-AI, CAP-AUDIT. Twin/AI consumers see accepted typed records only.

Unknown fields cannot enter clinical truth unvalidated. Unit/time/identity corruption is detected; schema drift suspends affected mappings; replay creates no duplicate fact; failed releases can be disabled without losing history. A candidate connector cannot call destructive endpoints. Approved round-trip loss reports retain every unmapped field disposition. These are specification requirements: no real hospital connector has been generated, tested or approved. Partner contracts, terminology packs, conformance suites and named approval authority remain open.

requirements.text: Forms the epidemiological intelligence layer of the Medical Passport ecosystem.
Potential matches require research-team verification before enrollment.
Supports international pediatric oncology trial discovery.
AI-generated matches require trial-site eligibility verification.
Measure pediatric neurosurgical outcomes and create governed research-ready longitudinal datasets.
Research processing requires appropriate authorization, consent where applicable, de-identification and auditability.
Coordinate clinical-trial participation without mixing investigational treatment with routine standard-of-care documentation.
Revision 2026-09-14 · EXT-RESEARCH · DRAFT_SPECIFICATION · CAP-RESEARCH · governed secondary analysis / population and longitudinal research · roadmap RESEARCH.

Use authorized longitudinal data to investigate patterns and generate hypotheses. Sources 1823/1826 already contain cohort matching, correlation and knowledge mining; 4649 contains research authorization/de-identification/audit. 1438's “anonymous” description is an intent, not proof of anonymity. 1915 research education remains educational. Extend shared governance and evidence contracts rather than merge all analytics into a single authority.
| Purpose | Scope and output | Authority boundary |
| Patient Analytics | individual trends/explanations | patient and care delegation |
| Clinical Analytics | clinician's authorized care cohort and outcomes | treating/clinical quality role |
| Provider Analytics | capacity, workload and operational quality | provider operations; no unnecessary clinical details |
| Population Analytics | aggregate patterns across authorized cohorts | population analysis release policy |
| Epidemiology | incidence, trends, surveillance methods | defined surveillance purpose and denominator |
| Research Analytics | protocol-specific hypothesis/outcome analyses | approved research governance |
| Public Health Reporting | authority-defined reporting dataset | recipient/jurisdiction-specific reporting basis |

Eurostat/government reporting is a separately versioned recipient contract; it is not an API granting general access to research data. Different purposes may share computation infrastructure while retaining independent permission, definitions and release policy.

Investigator defines protocol and estimand; data steward approves datasets; privacy/disclosure reviewer authorizes release; clinical/evidence reviewer evaluates implications. Patients/guardians provide consent when it is the applicable basis; other legal bases must be documented and reviewed rather than presumed.

Input references governed records: conditions, phenotype, longitudinal medication exposure, labs, comorbidities and outcomes. CohortSpec records inclusion/exclusion, index date, observation window, missingness, outcome definitions, versioned code lists, provenance, dataset release and permitted purpose. A hypertension study can join these authorized longitudinal dimensions; the resulting association is not automatically causal treatment evidence.

Functions include cohort discovery, phenotype clustering, treatment/outcome and disease-progression analysis, adverse-event signals, biomarker/population/therapy-response patterns, rare-disease patterns and hypothesis generation. Each output names method, denominator, bias/confounding limits and data completeness.

CAP-RESEARCH owns protocol, cohort/query version, governed dataset release, AnalysisRun and Hypothesis. Clinical stores retain originals; pseudonym linkage keys reside in a separately controlled service. Pseudonymization is not anonymization. Minimize fields, restrict rare/small groups, apply disclosure review and query-history controls to reduce differencing attacks. Privacy-preserving/federated/aggregate methods require their own evaluation and configured release policy; no universal safe cell threshold is assumed.

Proposed commands: registerProtocol, requestCohort, approveDatasetRelease, executeAnalysis, requestDisclosureReview, submitEvidenceReview. Events DatasetReleaseApproved, AnalysisCompleted, HypothesisSubmitted and EvidenceReleaseApproved carry opaque IDs, never row-level exports. A denied query must not reveal membership. Unauthorized jurisdiction, missing basis or expired release returns a refusal. Dependencies CAP-DATA, CAP-CONSENT, CAP-AI, CAP-AUDIT.

Patient data → authorized minimized/pseudonymized research dataset → Research AI → hypothesis → methodological and independent clinical validation appropriate to the claim → evidence release → Knowledge AI → separately validated Clinical AI/twin/pharmacology release.

A Hypothesis cannot enter the clinical knowledge pack as an established fact. EvidenceRelease records study/protocol, dataset/method versions, validation evidence, reviewer, applicability, limitations and expiry/review triggers. Conflicting results coexist with provenance. Promotion and rollback are explicit signed lifecycle actions.

The improvement loop is governed dataset → evaluation → approved research/training task → model candidate → validation → deployment approval → monitoring. Dataset reuse, model training and external-provider transfer each require an appropriate approved basis. Withdrawal and changed permissions invalidate future access and trigger governed retention/model-impact assessment; never promise that deleting one record erases its influence from a trained model.

Research AI cannot change treatment, dose, clinical facts or patient model release. Signals require validation; correlation is not causation. Prevent cross-tenant joins, membership leakage, small-cohort exports and uncontrolled researcher re-identification. Audit dataset access, approved query fingerprints, disclosure decisions and evidence release history; sensitive outputs remain in controlled storage.

Tests block unauthorized cohorts, disclosure bypass, expired governance, unapproved model training and hypothesis-to-care publication. Replays use exact cohort/data/code versions. Changing outcome definitions creates a new analysis. Clinical consumers accept only approved evidence releases applicable to their task. No research dataset, approved study, trained model or public reporting integration exists yet; methodology, jurisdiction decisions and independent governance remain open.

records.title: Shared CAP-SPECIALTY specification with explicit profiles

profiles.reason: 3061 retains ICU and lifelong follow-up; 3661 adds hypertension/prevention/electrophysiology; 4061 emphasizes ECG/MRI. One profile retains each scope.
Retain specific defect names, single-ventricle physiology, hemodynamics, procedures and explicit adult-congenital transition.
Retain named channelopathies, AV/conduction disorders, bradyarrhythmia, Holter/event monitoring and electrophysiology.
Symptoms, myocarditis, mechanical support, fluid status, hospitalization, transplant evaluation and function are complementary.
Workspace and coordination views share data but retain rehabilitation, research, genetics and ICU interfaces.
Dashboard, clinical core and orchestration layers differ; no duplicate patient stores or mandatory deployment-per-module inference.
Retain broad clinical domains plus explicit episode/assessment schema and workflows; local MVP wording does not expand EDHT P0.
Retain developmental/substance/family care, restricted summaries, passport and conditional adult transfer; no universal guardian or school access.
Retain allergy dashboard, immune integration, vaccine clearance, anaphylaxis, immunotherapy and transition across shared owners.
5002 extends baseline/recovery and multisystem phenotype; retain explicit vaccine-response and test-type detail from 4444.
Combined-immunity scope and neonatal SCID screening require linked but distinct screening, confirmation, escalation and definitive-treatment states.
Respiratory orchestration retains congenital/airway/rare disease, sleep, home ventilation and emergency/passport interfaces. A common workspace delegates clinical facts and orders to their owners.
Asthma profiles distinguish diagnosis, control, exacerbation, trigger inference, allergic context and signed action plan. Preserve biologics, age-appropriate framework and school disclosure.

CF shares a longitudinal profile while retaining CFTR-modulator eligibility, pancreatic/nutrition/endocrine/fertility context and exacerbation recovery. Molecular interpretation and medication orders remain separate.
Digestive orchestration preserves hepatology, pancreatic/motility/feeding/intestinal-failure care and nutrition with shared source owners and separate signed plans.

Retain IBD-unclassified/indeterminate terminology history, Crohn location/behavior, UC extent, monogenic immune context, growth and instrument-specific activity; no automatic scores or targeted treatment.
Retain named functional disorders and legacy Rome IV reference, evolving framework version, motility testing, continence and patient-reported burden.

Nutrition profiles retain feeding skills, micronutrients, formula/route and fluid/calorie units, PN composition/access, remaining bowel anatomy and adaptation. Orders and pump/compounding actions remain external authorized workflows.
Systemic disease orchestration retains all organ interfaces, specialty independence, evolving phenotype and adult handover; local MVP wording does not change global adult P0.
Retain subtype, active/limited joint counts, intra-articular procedure history, uveitis and growth, plans and guardian diaries.
One examination/map profile preserves laterality, effusion, tendon involvement, injection/surgery history, gait and observed versus rendered findings.
Systemic and renal lupus assessments are coordinated profiles; retain urinary/blood-pressure/biopsy/complement evidence, organ damage and renal relapse with separate clinical authority.
Preserve electrophysiology, muscle biopsy, swallowing/respiratory involvement, calcinosis and multidisciplinary rehabilitation.
Localized and systemic scope retains vascular/skin distribution, contracture, organ surveillance and change timeline without collapsing disease classifications.
Preserve vessel distribution/size, ocular and other organ contexts, biopsy, damage and recurrence.
Maintain diagnostic classification history and uncertain/evolving overlap phenotype; normalization never forces a diagnosis.
Keep patient/guardian attribution, school and social participation, sleep/fatigue and treatment burden even when inflammatory markers are normal.

One hematology orchestration profile retains hemostasis, marrow failure, apheresis, hemovigilance, immune/genetic interfaces and adult transition. It delegates authoritative results, blood-bank releases and treatment orders.

Retain anemia subtypes, reticulocyte response, iron/vitamin/renal/inflammatory context, oral/IV iron history and menstrual/GI blood loss as distinct clinical contexts; no automatic diagnosis or iron prescription.

Sickle-cell and thalassemia remain distinct disease profiles sharing longitudinal infrastructure. Retain carrier/newborn screening, acute chest/stroke/splenic risk, hydroxyurea context, alloantibodies, MRI iron, chelation and endocrine/bone outcomes.

Preserve hemophilia, von Willebrand and rare factor/fibrinogen/platelet-function disorders separately; inhibitor and non-factor therapy, home treatment, dental/surgery and menstrual bleeding context remain explicit.

Platelet/white-cell/multilineage marrow profiles retain qualitative platelet disease, cyclic neutropenia, named inherited syndromes, medication/toxin exposure, prophylaxis and transplant evaluation without equating every cytopenia.

HSCT coordination retains donor search/HLA, conditioning, engraftment, GVHD, immune recovery and lifelong complications. Donor identity/permissions are separate, and no matching score determines eligibility.
Venous/arterial/catheter/cerebral events, provoking factors, recurrence, post-thrombotic outcomes and genetic/acquired risk remain distinct; testing and anticoagulation decisions are specialist-led.

Oncology and CNS-specific orchestration are profiles of the shared specialty owner. Preserve tumor-specific interfaces, molecular evolution, rehabilitation, palliative and lifelong developmental care without fragmenting source records.

Multidisciplinary diagnostic integration retains specimen/surgical source, DNA/RNA/epigenetic context, lab/pathologist/report versions, external review and tumor-board evidence. Signed pathology and reclassification remain attributable.
ALL/AML/mixed-lineage profiles retain immunophenotype, cytogenetic/molecular risk, treatment phases and MRD assay/time-point/sensitivity context; missing MRD never implies remission.

Distinct glioma/embryonal/ependymal/sellar/optic-pathway tumor profiles retain molecular grouping, CSF/spinal staging, resection, endocrine/visual function and supportive care; stable imaging cannot erase visual decline.

Response, recurrence, toxicity and survivorship profiles retain criterion/version, discordant modalities, repeat molecular/biopsy evidence, cumulative exposure, secondary malignancy and lifelong follow-up; no invented schedule.

Educational communication and concurrent palliative/supportive care are separate specialty workflows. Preserve age-appropriate multilingual explanation, symptoms, care goals and family needs without implying treatment cessation.

Keep seizures/neurological deficits, endocrine/water-balance/growth, cognitive baseline, educational accommodations and hearing/vision outcomes as linked profiles with source attribution and minimum-necessary school disclosure.

CAR-T coordination uses a specialty profile and existing source owners; retain chain of identity/custody through collection, manufacturing, bridging, release and infusion. Manufacturing progress is not product-release authority.

Shared neurosurgical orchestration retains prenatal-to-adult scope, neuroendoscopy, neurotrauma, surgical planning, implants, neurocritical care and rehabilitation. Independent deployability remains an option; AI cannot determine indication or operative strategy.

Hydrocephalus and tumor-related CSF disease are clinical coordination profiles. Preserve ventricular/head-growth/development/vision, CSF diversion, external drainage/ETV and infection/revision context; actual device configuration stays with the device owner.
Preserve suture/syndromic phenotype, functional/cosmetic outcomes, airway/ophthalmic/neurodevelopment and dental/orthodontic reconstruction context within one craniofacial profile.

Neural-tube and other congenital disorders retain prenatal linkage, lesion level/closure, motor/sensory, kidney/bladder/bowel, skin, nutrition, education and social care. Verified maternal-child linkage does not merge identities or permissions.
Retain malformation classification, brainstem/swallowing/sleep-breathing, syrinx, CSF-flow imaging, decompression complications and response surveillance.

Distinct syrinx, injury, tethering, dysraphism and spinal-tumor profiles retain anatomy/measurements, neurological and renal/urodynamic function, retethering, pathology and rehabilitation; they are not synonymous diagnoses.

Preserve treatment-failure history, video-EEG, functional/structural imaging, genetic/metabolic and neuropsychology context, surgical hypothesis, conference, consent and separately authorized decision; neither AI nor a test establishes eligibility alone.

Functional/spasticity/dystonia/pain/epilepsy therapy coordination retains goals, intrathecal therapy, implantation/programming history, battery and functional outcomes while device and medication owners retain their facts.

Neurovascular and intracranial-bleeding profiles retain AVM/cavernous/aneurysm/moyamoya, angiography, coagulation/anticoagulant/hemophilia context and endovascular/radiosurgical outcomes. No autonomous hemostatic or reversal action.

Severe injury and concussion retain mechanism/time, consciousness/amnesia, ICU/imaging and school/cognitive recovery. Return-to-learn and return-to-activity require distinct clinician clearance; a low automated risk signal cannot exclude acute injury.
Preserve wound/CNS/shunt infection, CSF leak/hemorrhage, microbiology/resistance, device removal/replacement, ICU/reoperation and attributable resolution versus suspected findings.

One neonatal orchestration owner coordinates delivery-room, term/preterm, ICU, congenital and lifelong developmental profiles. Maternal and infant records remain distinct, and historical local MVP claims do not authorize deployment.
Preserve extremely/very/moderate preterm contexts, growth, respiratory support, neurodevelopment and complication follow-up with appropriate age/reference applicability.

NICU coordination retains high-flow and high-frequency ventilation as distinct modalities alongside CPAP, hemodynamic monitoring, infection control and nutrition. Source observations and prescribed settings remain separate from control.
Keep transient tachypnea, distress, meconium aspiration, persistent pulmonary hypertension, BPD and apnea distinct with ventilation/oxygen history and clinical interpretation.
Early/late-onset and congenital infection/meningitis remain distinct episode contexts; microbiology, antibiotics and response retain source timing and clinical diagnosis authority.

Jaundice profile coordinates source bilirubin, age/gestation, phototherapy and separately authorized exchange-transfusion context. No thresholds or treatment recommendation are inferred from a legacy title.

Screening, confirmatory evaluation and established congenital diagnosis are distinct states. Preserve metabolic/hearing/cardiac, chromosomal/rare/genomic and organ-specific anomalies plus family counseling without treating a screen as diagnosis.

Preserve breastfeeding, donor milk, fortification, enteral/parenteral routes, tolerance and growth. Orders/formula changes and administration remain separately authorized; donor product provenance is not blanket donor access.

Growth/development and complications retain measurement time/technique, weight/length/head circumference and selected reference release. Historical WHO wording does not prove suitability for every gestational age.
Preserve reflex/tone examination, seizures, HIE, hemorrhage/leukomalacia and source neuroimaging without collapsing distinct injury phenotypes into a single AI label.
Cardiac neonatal profile links congenital diagnoses and echo/monitoring source data to specialist review using existing clinical/imaging/device owners.

Congenital malformations, appendicitis and hernia are separate specialty profiles. Preserve congenital imaging/follow-up, appendiceal histology/recovery and inguinal, umbilical and diaphragmatic anatomy without collapsing urgency or treatment pathways.

Wound infection, bleeding, sepsis, reoperation and recovery extend musculoskeletal infection profiles. Preserve osteomyelitis, septic arthritis, implant infection, aspiration, cultures/susceptibility, duration, response and recurrence. Suspected and confirmed episodes differ; prescribing remains with medication authority.

Surgical dashboard and orthopedic core/hub compose shared source-owned clinical services. Preserve examination, congenital/acquired disease, growth, hip/spine/limb/foot/hand, trauma, surgery, orthotics/prosthetics, pain, outcomes and MVP-versus-expansion scope. Modular deployment remains optional; local MVP labels do not authorize release.

Functional examination retains posture, gait, joint stability, range of motion, strength/tone, limb alignment/length, pain and device use with examiner/method/age. Baseline, growth and postoperative changes must remain distinguishable from model-generated trends.

Congenital orthopedics and skeletal dysplasia share longitudinal coordination with distinct genetic/phenotypic profiles. Preserve prenatal/neonatal context, proportions, craniofacial, respiratory and neurological associations, imaging/molecular provenance, casting/orthotics and adult transition without merging maternal identity or genetic consent.

Hip development, dysplasia and preservation retain laterality, screening/instability, imaging methods/measurements, gait, bracing/casting, surgery and skeletal-growth surveillance. Measurements require age/method context and never independently authorize surgery.

Scoliosis, kyphosis/lordosis and congenital, neuromuscular and syndromic deformity remain distinct profiles. Preserve curve method, source acquisition, maturity/growth, brace/physiotherapy and operative outcomes; incompatible images cannot substantiate progression automatically.

Limb discrepancy/deformity and growth-plate surveillance preserve length, rotation, mechanical axis, injury site/classification, growth arrest and serial correction context. Guided growth, lengthening, osteotomy and fixation remain specialist decisions; fracture healing does not close growth surveillance.

Foot/ankle and upper-extremity profiles retain separate anatomy: clubfoot/flatfoot/cavus/toes/instability versus congenital limb differences, shoulder/elbow/wrist/hand, strength and sensation. Preserve casting, recurrence, splints, orthotics, occupational therapy and functional outcomes.

Fracture/complex high-energy injury profiles preserve mechanism, dislocation, open fracture, pelvic/soft-tissue damage, neurovascular assessment, reduction, temporary stabilization and definitive fixation. Growth-plate/remodeling, healing, implant/wound/infection and return-to-activity context remain explicit; no automated injury exclusion.

Sports care retains athlete/training context, acute versus overuse and apophyseal/bone-stress injury, nutrition/endocrine associations, load modification, rehab, recurrence and functional tests. A recovery trajectory cannot issue return-to-sport permission.

Bone health preserves recurrent fracture/density, vitamin D/calcium/phosphate, genetic/endocrine/renal/nutritional context, medication and mobility. Lab results remain source-owned with units and age context; no universal pediatric treatment threshold is inferred.

Musculoskeletal oncology retains tumor anatomy, biopsy, histology/molecular evidence, staging reference, systemic treatment, resection/reconstruction, limb preservation, prosthesis and recurrence/function. This coordinates existing oncology and pathology authority rather than creating a second staging truth.

Acute/chronic/postoperative pain retains anatomical severity, sleep/school/function, medication, nonpharmacologic/psychological therapies and patient outcomes. Clinical medication and intervention decisions are distinct from tracking or inferred recovery.

Trauma core/polytrauma and recovery hub share orchestration across prehospital, multisystem organs, imaging/lab, procedures, ICU, blood products, sports and rehabilitation. One episode timeline preserves source-specific times and clinician prioritization. Independent services and future wearables/robotics/twin/research are retained without claiming implemented coverage.

Thoracic/abdominal profiles retain pulmonary/pleural/cardiac, liver/spleen/kidney/gastrointestinal/pancreatic/pelvic injury, monitoring, nonoperative, surgical and interventional contexts with attributable decisions; automated summaries never determine treatment priority.

Complex wounds and burns preserve location/tissue/contamination/neurovascular status, debridement/closure/reconstruction versus burn depth/extent, airway/fluid/graft context. Preserve infection/scar/contracture, pain, nutrition, psychological support and growth-related function; no unvalidated resuscitation instructions are generated.

Cardiorespiratory medical safety and nutrition are separate athlete health profiles. Preserve exercise symptoms/syncope/family history, specialist restrictions/emergency plan, growth/energy/iron/bone and menstrual context where appropriate. Health precedes performance; coach access does not authorize sensitive adolescent disclosures.

Rehabilitation coordination retains temporary/permanent impairment, mobility/strength/balance, daily living, cognition/communication/swallowing, goals, pain and school/home/social participation; it composes therapy-specific plans and source-owned devices.

Clinical motion assessment retains observational versus instrumented gait, kinematics/kinetics, muscle activity, speed/endurance, orthotic/surgical context and longitudinal comparison. Raw acquisition stays device-owned; methods, units, anatomical frame and calibration must be compatible before comparison or twin inference.

Functional outcomes preserve mobility/self-care/communication, school/social/recreation, sleep/pain/fatigue, independence and caregiver assistance. Patient and guardian reports retain respondent and instrument/version; proxy and patient perspectives remain distinct and missing values are not imputed independence.

Revision 2026-09-14 · EXT-TWIN · DRAFT_SPECIFICATION · CAP-TWIN · shared clinical model / patient state · roadmap RESEARCH.

Organize patient representation, visualization and model outputs in one versioned system. Hundreds of specialty titles mention twins; these become candidate profiles, not separate infrastructure. Sources 1224 and 1876 describe hospital/resource operations and remain operational models. A workflow model of a physician (1225) is also separate from patient physiology. Search alternatives and preservation decisions are in [dossier](new_module_proposals.json) and [semantic diffs](semantic_diffs.json).
| Level | Input | Output and release gate |
| 1 Digital Patient Representation | authorized clinical records and provenance | chronological representation with conflicting/missing facts retained |
| 2 Anatomical / Organ System Visualization | generic atlas or validated imaging-derived geometry | labelled body/organ view; provenance required for patient-derived claims |
| 3 Patient-specific physiological state | timed labs, device signals, clinical observations | measured state plus separately typed inferred estimates; calibration/time alignment gate |
| 4 Disease-state models | diagnoses, clinical assessments, longitudinal evidence | disease-specific model instance with validated intended use and uncertainty |
| 5 Treatment-response models | reconciled therapy exposures and outcomes | prediction with explicit horizon, context and applicability |
| 6 Scenario simulation | frozen state and user-selected hypothetical intervention | simulated trajectories, assumptions and alternatives; no clinical fact writes |
| 7 Longitudinal patient-specific model | successive approved snapshots and model releases | versioned history, drift/invalidation, comparison and replay |

A level is enabled only after its own data and validation gates. Passing level 1 does not imply availability of levels 3–7. Missing later levels are displayed as unavailable. An individual parameter fit is a versioned model change with validation, not permission for autonomous learning.

Patients can view authorized summaries and mark reported context; clinicians interpret clinical views; imaging specialists validate derived anatomy; model stewards validate model releases. Guardian/delegation access follows age, scope and transition rules. Clinical data owners retain facts; CAP-TWIN owns TwinSnapshot, ModelInstance, ScenarioRun and derived anatomy references. Shared stores retain imaging, medication and device records.

Create snapshot → check required inputs → select approved profile/model → calculate → persist typed output → reviewer disposition → monitor invalidation. Snapshot includes tenant/patient, time range, consent/purpose, source IDs/versions, missingness, model release and profile. ScenarioRun includes parameters, baseline, horizon, uncertainty representation, computation version and epistemic_status SIMULATED. No synthetic value replaces an Observation.

Support references to CT, MRI, PET/CT, X-ray, ultrasound, OCT and future modalities. Store study/series/instance identifiers, acquisition time, modality, geometry/coordinate frame, derivation/segmentation method and review status. FHIR ImagingStudy/DiagnosticReport/Observation/Provenance are candidate linkage resources; DICOM objects remain under imaging ownership.

Generic anatomy always displays “generic anatomy”. Patient-derived anatomy requires traceable patient imaging, registration/segmentation provenance and acceptance by the appropriate workflow; a generic atlas cannot acquire that label because the patient name is displayed. De-identify exported images, including embedded metadata, according to the authorized workflow.

Provide organ/system highlighting, clinical timeline, lab overlays, biomarker state, device signals, disease activity and therapy exposure. Spatial and temporal uncertainty, stale source data and unavailable organ models stay visible.

Proposed commands: createTwinSnapshot, evaluateModel, runScenario, invalidateDerivedOutputs, compareSnapshots. Query returns level availability and typed artifacts. Events TwinSnapshotCreated, ScenarioCompleted, DerivedOutputInvalidated carry IDs/versions only. Reject wrong patient/tenant, incompatible profile, stale input version and unsupported model with explicit error codes. Retries are idempotent; asynchronous cancellation must not publish a partial result as complete. Dependencies CAP-DATA, CAP-AI, CAP-IMAGING, CAP-DEVICES, CAP-CONSENT; connected medication and specialty profiles supply authorized references.

AI may estimate and explain within a validated task; it neither diagnoses autonomously nor prescribes. Separate OBSERVED, MEASURED, REPORTED, CLINICIAN_ASSESSED, INFERRED, PREDICTED and SIMULATED. Confidence measures mean only what the model's evaluation supports; absent confidence is unknown. Model outage offers an authorized earlier snapshot explicitly marked stale, or abstains. Cross-patient joins, device clock drift and incomplete imaging must block patient-specific inference. Logs capture model/context hashes, failures, latency and reviewer action with patient details excluded.

Verify all seven level states; source updates invalidate downstream outputs without deleting history; a scenario never changes facts or orders; replay uses exact recorded versions. Test generic/patient-derived labelling, imaging identifier mismatch, longitudinal comparison, consent revocation and accessible non-3D rendering. All numerical physiology, disease and response models require specialist validation and intended-use evidence. This draft establishes contracts; it supplies no validated patient simulator. Revision 2026-09-14 · EXT-VISUAL · DRAFT_SPECIFICATION · CAP-TWIN · presentation of evidence and derived clinical models · roadmap RESEARCH.

Present possible therapy effects on organs, systems, pathways, laboratory markers and known risk areas with their evidence. Existing organ models, multisystem monitoring and therapy-exposure concepts provide inputs; this extension adds a common display contract. It does not justify a new clinical truth store. See [alternatives](new_module_proposals.json). An animation is an explanation of an identified evidence/model result, not proof that a physiological effect occurred.

An authorized clinician selects reconciled therapy and a patient-context version; the view resolves known pharmacology, patient context, evidence and approved model outputs. A patient may receive a restricted explanatory view subject to access policy and clinician-reviewed content. An educator may use an explicitly generic case. Selecting a medicine for a scenario never initiates a prescription.

Choose context → choose observed history or hypothetical scenario → resolve evidence → render overlays → inspect source/assumptions → compare timeline or scenario. Scenario mode remains visible during navigation, sharing and export.
CAP-TWIN owns ViewComposition, referencing facts from CAP-DATA, images from CAP-IMAGING and derived assessments from CAP-CDS. No independent duplicate Observation is created.

Each Overlay contains organ/system/pathway key, sourceArtifactId, epistemic_status, evidence reference/version, contextSnapshotId, effective time, model/assumption references where applicable, uncertainty, staleness and anatomy provenance.

OBSERVED denotes a documented observation; MEASURED a measured quantity with unit/method; INFERRED a derived interpretation; PREDICTED a forecast; SIMULATED a hypothetical scenario. REPORTED and CLINICIAN_ASSESSED remain available when inherited from the clinical data contract. Never change status based on display styling. Epistemic status and clinical validation status are independent.

Interactive body and organ/system highlighting have keyboard equivalents. A timeline synchronizes lab overlays, biomarkers, device signals, disease activity and therapy exposure while displaying missing intervals and differing time resolutions. A side panel lists affected structures, source, evidence strength as defined by that source, assumptions and exclusions. Actual values and hypothetical curves use labels, legends and patterns, not colour alone. Unknown effects display unknown, not green or zero.

Generic anatomy is labelled throughout. Patient-derived geometry references acquisition and accepted derivation; clinically irrelevant visual detail cannot imply unavailable precision. CT/MRI/PET-CT/X-ray/ultrasound/OCT links open the underlying authorized imaging workflow. A textual/table alternative carries the same information, including uncertainty.

Proposed read operations: getTreatmentImpactView and getOverlayEvidence. Scenario computation delegates to CAP-TWIN; assessment to CAP-CDS. Events ViewContextChanged and ViewInvalidated contain opaque version references. Cache keys include tenant, purpose, authorization scope, context and evidence/model releases. Recheck authorization before export; cached content is invalidated after revocation.

A missing asset switches to the accessible list. Source/model mismatch hides the affected overlay and explains the failure. Stale patient context blocks a new patient-specific scenario. Partial retrieval is visibly partial; animation timing must never imply a validated biological time course unless such a model was actually used.
## Security, clinical safety and AI boundary

The viewer cannot mutate clinical facts, medication orders or model releases. AI may summarize supported overlays with clickable evidence; unsupported explanations are omitted. Limit visible family/genomic information and external provider transfers. Export includes scenario/generic labels, creation time and source versions. Log access and export decisions without duplicating medical content.

Tests must preserve all epistemic labels across view, screenshot/export and API output; generic geometry must never be labelled patient-derived. Screen-reader and keyboard paths must expose all warnings. Selecting a drug produces no medication mutation. A confidence-free result is shown as uncertainty unknown. Stale or revoked results disappear from newly authorized queries. Usability and clinician comprehension testing must establish that users distinguish observed effects from scenarios. No visual application or animation is implemented in this stage.
